title: CRIS-b: A High-Speed Unified Modulo Reduction Algorithm and Hardware Architecture for CRYSTALS-Kyber
problem: Modulo reduction is a critical bottleneck in post-quantum cryptography (CRYSTALS-Kyber). Conventional Barrett algorithm suffers from size expansion of intermediate values, limiting clock frequency and throughput in hardware implementations.
motivation: Post-quantum cryptographic standards like Kyber require efficient hardware implementations for practical deployment. Modulo reduction must be accelerated without sacrificing reliability or architectural compatibility.
method: CRIS-b algorithm solves a critical efficiency problem in the Barrett method, which computes remainders after division (modulo reduction)—the standard approach produces intermediate values that grow too large, slowing down hardware implementations. It uses conditional switching to choose between different calculation methods at each step, keeping intermediate results smaller and enabling faster execution. Unlike conventional approaches, CRIS-b handles both positive and negative numbers in a single unified process, which is necessary for the mathematical transformations (NTT butterfly operations) used in CRYSTALS-Kyber post-quantum encryption. The algorithm was implemented on an Artix-7 FPGA (a reprogrammable hardware processor).
key_novelty: CRIS-b eliminates the size-expansion bottleneck of modulo reduction by conditionally switching between calculation methods, enabling unified handling of both positive and negative numbers needed for post-quantum encryption.
contributions: 351.62 MHz maximum clock frequency on Artix-7 FPGA (35.24% faster than prior SOTA)
Handles both positive and negative spectrum for NTT butterfly operations
Conditional R-index switching technique reducing intermediate value expansion
Unified architecture eliminating need for separate reduction paths
limitations: FPGA-only implementation; ASIC synthesis results not provided
Limited to Artix-7 platform; scaling to other FPGA families not discussed
No power consumption or area metrics provided
Comparison limited to frequency; energy efficiency (pJ/cycle) not analyzed
Does not address full Kyber pipeline integration or end-to-end cryptographic operations
